title: Lectura en voz alta: la vida diaria

exercises.text: Ojalá que mi hermana pueda venir a Oaxaca para que mis papás conozcan por fin a su nieto.
exercises.meaningEn: I hope my sister can come to Oaxaca so that my parents can finally meet their grandson.

glosses.ojalá: I hope — always takes the subjunctive
glosses.que: that (ojalá que = I hope that; para que = so that)
glosses.pueda: can — present subjunctive of poder, after ojalá
glosses.a: to (a Oaxaca); before a person, a is not translated (a su nieto)
glosses.oaxaca: Oaxaca (state and city in southern Mexico)
glosses.conozcan: (they) meet — present subjunctive of conocer, after para que

note.en: Ojalá always takes the subjunctive. The word que after it is optional: ojalá pueda or ojalá que pueda.
note.es: Ojalá siempre lleva subjuntivo. La palabra que después es opcional: ojalá pueda u ojalá que pueda.

exercises.text: ¿Qué tal tu fin de semana? Espero que hayas podido descansar un poco.
exercises.meaningEn: How was your weekend? I hope you were able to rest a little.

exercises.text: Quisiera agendar una cita, aunque sea con otro doctor, porque me duele la garganta y tengo la voz ronca.
exercises.meaningEn: I would like to book an appointment, even if it is with a different doctor, because my throat hurts and my voice is hoarse.

glosses.quisiera: I would like — imperfect subjunctive of querer (polite)
glosses.aunque: even if (+ subjunctive: it does not matter)
glosses.sea: it is — present subjunctive of ser, after aunque
glosses.duele: hurts — 3rd person of doler (me duele = it hurts me)

note.en: Quisiera is the imperfect subjunctive of querer. It makes a request more polite, like "I would like".
note.es: Quisiera es el imperfecto de subjuntivo de querer. Vuelve la petición más cortés.

exercises.text: Dile al doctor que tengo gripa y que me recete algo que no me dé sueño.
exercises.meaningEn: Tell the doctor that I have the flu and that he should prescribe me something that does not make me drowsy.

glosses.dile: tell him/her — tú command of decir + le
glosses.que: that (dile que = tell him that; algo que = something that)
glosses.me: me, to me (me recete = prescribe me; me dé = make me)
glosses.dé: gives — present subjunctive of dar (dar sueño = make drowsy)

note.en: After dile que, use the indicative to give information (tengo gripa). Use the subjunctive to ask for an action (me recete).
note.es: Después de dile que, usa indicativo para informar (tengo gripa). Usa subjuntivo para pedir una acción (me recete).

exercises.text: Antes de que se te acabe la medicina, pídele otra receta a la doctora para no quedarte sin ella.
exercises.meaningEn: Before you run out of medicine, ask the doctor for another prescription so that you do not end up without it.

glosses.se: part of acabarse (se te acabe = you run out)
glosses.te: you (se te acabe = you run out)
glosses.acabe: runs out — present subjunctive of acabarse, after antes de que
glosses.pídele: ask him/her for — tú command of pedir + le
glosses.para: to, in order to (para + infinitive: same subject)
glosses.quedarte: to end up, to be left — infinitive quedarse + te

exercises.text: El doctor me checó la presión y me dijo que, a menos que bajara de peso, tendría que tomar pastillas.
exercises.meaningEn: The doctor checked my blood pressure and told me that, unless I lost weight, I would have to take pills.

glosses.me: me (me checó = checked me; me dijo = told me)
glosses.checó: checked — 3rd person preterite of checar (Mexican for revisar)
glosses.dijo: told, said — 3rd person preterite of decir
glosses.que: that (me dijo que = told me that; a menos que = unless)
glosses.bajara: (I) lost, went down — imperfect subjunctive of bajar, after a menos que
glosses.tendría: I would have — conditional of tener (tendría que = would have to)

note.en: After a past verb such as me dijo que, the subjunctive is usually in the imperfect: a menos que bajara. The result uses the conditional: tendría.
note.es: Después de un verbo en pasado como me dijo que, el subjuntivo suele ir en imperfecto (a menos que bajara) y el resultado en condicional (tendría).

exercises.text: Avísame en cuanto salgas de la consulta para que pase por ti.
exercises.meaningEn: Let me know as soon as you leave the appointment so that I can pick you up.

exercises.text: ¡Qué bueno que ya haya dejado de llover! Si siguiera lloviendo así, no podríamos hacer la carne asada el domingo.
exercises.meaningEn: How good that it has already stopped raining! If it kept raining like that, we could not have the cookout on Sunday.

glosses.qué: how (¡qué bueno que…! = how good that…!)
glosses.haya: has — present subjunctive of haber (haya dejado = has stopped)
glosses.dejado: stopped — past participle of dejar (dejar de = stop)
glosses.siguiera: (it) continued — imperfect subjunctive of seguir, after si
glosses.lloviendo: raining — gerund of llover (seguir lloviendo = keep raining)
glosses.asada: grilled (carne asada = grilled beef, a Mexican cookout)

exercises.text: Mi mamá quiere que vayamos a Guadalajara el próximo año, aunque no haya vuelos baratos.
exercises.meaningEn: My mom wants us to go to Guadalajara next year, even if there are no cheap flights.

glosses.quiere: wants — 3rd person of querer; + que + subjunctive
glosses.vayamos: we go — present subjunctive of ir, after quiere que
glosses.aunque: even if (+ subjunctive: it may be true)
glosses.haya: there are — present subjunctive of haber, after aunque

exercises.text: Me encantaría que vinieras con nosotros a Xochimilco el sábado, a menos que ya tengas planes con tu familia.
exercises.meaningEn: I would love for you to come with us to Xochimilco on Saturday, unless you already have plans with your family.

glosses.me: to me (me encantaría = I would love)
glosses.encantaría: would love — conditional of encantar; + que + subjunctive
glosses.que: that (me encantaría que; a menos que = unless)
glosses.vinieras: you came — imperfect subjunctive of venir, after me encantaría que
glosses.a: to (a Xochimilco); a menos que = unless
glosses.xochimilco: Xochimilco (area of canals and boats in Mexico City)
glosses.tengas: (you) have — present subjunctive of tener, after a menos que

note.en: The letter x has two sounds in Mexican names. At the start of Xochimilco, it sounds like s. In Oaxaca and México, it sounds like j.
note.es: La letra x tiene dos sonidos en nombres mexicanos. Al inicio de Xochimilco suena como s. En Oaxaca y México suena como j.

exercises.text: Si no me hubieran checado la presión, no me habría enterado de que la tengo tan alta.
exercises.meaningEn: If they had not checked my blood pressure, I would not have found out that it is so high.

glosses.me: me (me hubieran checado = checked me; me habría enterado = I found out)
glosses.hubieran: (they) had — pluperfect subjunctive of haber, after si
glosses.la: the (la presión); it (la tengo = I have it)
glosses.enterado: found out — past participle of enterarse

exercises.text: Mi tío me pidió que recogiera sus medicinas antes de que cerraran la farmacia.
exercises.meaningEn: My uncle asked me to pick up his medicine before they closed the pharmacy.

exercises.text: Dudo que el doctor pueda atenderte hoy, pero la recepcionista dijo que tal vez haya espacio.
exercises.meaningEn: I doubt that the doctor can see you today, but the receptionist said there might be an opening.

glosses.dudo: I doubt — 1st person of dudar; takes the subjunctive
glosses.pueda: can — present subjunctive of poder, after dudo que
glosses.atenderte: to see you, to attend to you (atender + te)
glosses.haya: there is — present subjunctive of haber, after tal vez

exercises.text: El portero atajó tres penales como si fuera lo más fácil del mundo, y todo el estadio se paró.
exercises.meaningEn: The goalkeeper saved three penalty kicks as if it were the easiest thing in the world, and the whole stadium stood up.

glosses.atajó: stopped, saved — 3rd person preterite of atajar
glosses.fuera: (it) were — imperfect subjunctive of ser, after como si
glosses.lo: the (lo más fácil = the easiest thing)
glosses.del: of the (de + el); del mundo = in the world
glosses.paró: stood up — preterite of pararse (in Mexico: to stand up)

note.en: In Mexico, pararse often means to stand up: todo el estadio se paró. In Spain, pararse usually means to stop.
note.es: En México, pararse suele significar ponerse de pie: todo el estadio se paró. En España suele significar detenerse.
